Suggested criterion: mark when a consonant or vowel letter is inserted, deleted or replaced so that a different word is read (savair→sarvair, kṣaṇisya→kṣīṇasya, tuddvāha→tuddāha: u2 would then carry "on a conjectural reading" at the end of the sentence, u32 too); do not mark pure anusvāra or diacritic restorations (idra, arśāsi, pramehiṇa, masikā), which are the print's regular habit. Not patched because it is a book-wide policy call.

summary: Reviewed 41 units of Śārīrasthāna ch11 (Vikṛtavijñānīya, fatal-sign list) against the printed Sanskrit and Devanagari. The draft is careful: damaged units (11, 13, 17, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30) are handled per glossary (unsplit, unclear, conjectural mark, low confidence), identifications are tagged and hedged, nothing is added to the prognostic statements. Real errors: u37 (and u2 cauraso flag) treats a Devanagari hiatus (कूर्मइव, चउरसो) as a typo, so u37 wrongly carries the conjectural mark; u21 drops the printed ā of rujā from `words` and silently restores pārśvāṅga; u17 Hindi 'असरा'. Minor: Hindi पान for drinks, 'क्षीण होने पर', वसा gloss, muṣka as अण्डकोष, 'अति,' as a list item, u3 formula wording, u29 hedge, u41 Hindi lacks the modern name, gram of unstated-noun accusatives. Human decisions: conjectural-mark criterion for the silent restorations (u2, u9, u20, u32, u34), tulyaḥ scope over u22-24, tud versus tṛḍ in u32. No identification judged wrong. No regrouping needed (grouping notes are sensible; u3 introduces u4, whose nihanti governs the accusatives, u41 states hanti).
glossary_suggestions: p02 ch11: 'bhavati cātra' = 'And on this matter there is:' (already fixed; applied in u3).
IAST 'ai'/'au' hiatus confirmed again in p02 ch11 (u2 चउरसो = ca uraso, u37 कूर्मइव = kūrma iva); never a typo flag or conjectural mark.

Conjectural-mark criterion proposed: mark letter-level restorations that change the word read (savair→sarvair, kṣaṇisya→kṣīṇasya, tuddvāha→tuddāha); do not mark pure anusvāra/diacritic restorations (idra→indra, arśāsi→arśāṃsi, pramehiṇa→pramehiṇam, masikā→maṣikā). Owner to decide.
Hindi muṣka/vṛṣaṇa = वृषण (अण्डकोष is the scrotum); Hindi vasā = वसा यानी मांस की चर्बी; Hindi drinks = पेय (not पान); Hindi grīvā = गर्दन; asra = अस्र यानी रक्त या आँसू.
Adjectives standing for an unstated person/thing in -am (acc. sg.) carry no gender in gram (sweep applied to p02 ch11 u5-u41).

srasta-pāyu = slipped anus, probably prolapse of the anus or rectum (hedged in both languages); ghurghuraka = probably the death rattle; jaṭhara in the fatal list = probably an ascites-type belly disease (jalodara), Hindi जलोदर प्रकार का.
OPEN p02 ch11: u22-u24 scope of tulyaḥ ('with' vs 'similar to'); u32 tud-dāha vs tṛḍ-dāha; u25 ghana-vedanaḥ parse; u6 akṣāma kept as printed.
